body.statement: If the independently specified oracle-instance \(\mathsf X_{\mathrm{phys}}=(x_{\mathrm{str}},\mathcal O_{\mathrm{src}})\) admits at least one uniform acquisition certificate \(E\) with \(\operatorname{Acc}(Q,E;G)=1\), then the minimum defining \(\operatorname{Opt}\) is attained by the lexicographically first canonical uniform certificate \(E^{\star}\). Exhaustive enumeration of certificates of length at most \(B_{\mathrm{cert}}\), with cached oracle replies, outputs \(E^{\star}\), its protocol masks, exact \(|\mathrm{LIT}|\)-bit slice labels, source masks, factor-ownership masks, and one uniform finite restriction transcript schema per factor. Its time is \(2^{O(B_{\mathrm{cert}})}\operatorname{poly}(N_{\mathrm{in}}+N_{E^{\star}}+N_{\mathcal O})\), where \(N_{\mathcal O}\) charges every issued protocol query and returned law-handle and support-table bit. The verifier executes complete unconditional \(\operatorname{CTFIDU}^{+}\) on the decoded oracle-backed source collection. No bounded-treewidth runtime or optimum over arbitrary nonuniform acquired collections is claimed.
body.justification: The theorem retains exact cost optimization while exposing both the assignment-sensitive certificate size and every source-law or support access in the computational model.
body.gap: Akbari, Etesami, and Kiyavash (2025), Theorem 1 on page 5 and Lemma 3 on page 8, reduce a connected ordinary \(Q[S]\) target to one intervention and a hedge-hitting problem; Lemma 7 on page 12 certifies their exact Algorithm 2, and Proposition 3 on page 16 certifies their general-target Algorithm 3. Those results optimize ordinary intervention sets under fixed \(Q[S]\) source-family semantics, not oracle-explicit SELECT-RAND-CTF-RAND-READ protocols with reusable counterfactual slices and branch-labelled certificates.
body.consumer: Park and Lee's counterfactual structural causal bandit can compare the exact acquisition prices of finite reward-law protocols without treating source support as free hidden input.
body.proof_tex:
By Lemma \(\mathrm{Canonical\ certificate\ bound}\), the set
\[
 \mathcal F_B=\{E:N_E\le B_{\mathrm{cert}},\ \operatorname{Acc}(Q,E;G)=1\}
\]
is nonempty and contains a certificate whose cost is no larger than that of every accepting uniform certificate.  Hence its lexicographically first minimum-cost member is exactly \(E^{\star}\), and the definition of \(\operatorname{Opt}\) gives
\[
 \operatorname{Cost}(E^{\star})
 =\min_{E\in\mathcal F_B}\operatorname{Cost}(E)
 =\operatorname{Opt}.
\]

There are
\[
 \sum_{q=0}^{B_{\mathrm{cert}}}2^q
 <2^{B_{\mathrm{cert}}+1}
\]
binary strings of length at most \(B_{\mathrm{cert}}\).  Enumerate them in length-lexicographic order.  The operational predicate is total: it rejects malformed strings and, for a well-formed string, checks the protocol, label, support, source, ownership, and transcript clauses before executing the complete unconditional procedure on the decoded collection.  Cache the reply of \(\mathcal O_{\mathrm{src}}\) by protocol mask, so each distinct queried protocol is charged once during this optimization execution.

For a well-formed candidate, the number of assignment and equality-type branches is at most exponential in \(L=|\mathrm{LIT}|\).  Since \(k\ge1\), the displayed formula for \(B_{\mathrm{cert}}\) gives \(L\le B_{\mathrm{cert}}\).  Each fixed branch and source transcript has at most \(n\) restrictions, each checked by graph traversal and literal comparison.  Thus both complete branch enumeration and transcript verification take \(2^{O(B_{\mathrm{cert}})}\) times a polynomial in their explicit structural and oracle inputs.  Multiplication by the fewer than \(2^{B_{\mathrm{cert}}+1}\) candidate strings leaves the form \(2^{O(B_{\mathrm{cert}})}\).  Reading all oracle replies costs a polynomial in their total charged length \(N_{\mathcal O}\); moreover \(B_{\mathrm{cert}}\) and \(N_{E^{\star}}\) are polynomially bounded by \(N_{\mathrm{in}}\) by the canonical-certificate lemma.  This yields
\[
 2^{O(B_{\mathrm{cert}})}
 \operatorname{poly}(N_{\mathrm{in}}+N_{E^{\star}}+N_{\mathcal O}).
\]

Exact addition and comparison of nonnegative binary rationals are polynomial in their encoded bit lengths.  Retain the least cost encountered and break ties lexicographically.  Decoding the winning string outputs exactly its protocol, literal, source, ownership, and transcript fields.  The acceptance test itself executes the complete oracle-backed \(\operatorname{CTFIDU}^{+}\) run, so the output is an identification certificate for the stated uniform class, not a scalar functional and not a certificate for arbitrary nonuniform source switching.
